title: Fourth difference: repentance required—ordinary for venial; singular after David- and Peter-like falls
source_text: XLIII. Quarto differre dicit peccata mortalia & venialia, ratione poenitentiae ad eorum remissionem requisitae. Primo, quia ordinarium & quotidianum poenitentiae exercitium gratiose a Deo acceptatur, & pro sufficienti habetur ad expurganda peccata venialia. Sed sicut ipsa peccata mortalia sunt gravia, horrenda, & in vitae Chri-stianae cursu rara & extraordinaria; ita poenitentia quae ad ea expurganda necessario re-quiritur, singularis, magis accurata, & extraordinaria esse debet; qualis fuit Davidis post adulterium & homicidium, & Petri post Christi abnegationem.
pass_a_gloss: Fourthly he says mortal and venial sins differ by reason of the repentance required for their remission. First, because the ordinary and daily exercise of repentance is graciously accepted by God and held sufficient for purging venial sins. But just as mortal sins themselves are grave, dreadful, and in the course of the Christian life rare and extraordinary, so the repentance which is necessarily required for purging them ought to be singular, more exact, and extraordinary; such as was David’s after adultery and homicide, and Peter’s after the denial of Christ.
pass_b_english: Daily ordinary repentance clears venial faults.
Mortal falls demand rare, exact, extraordinary repentance—David after adultery and murder; Peter after denial.

choices.why: Ordinary repentance is enough for venial, not for capital falls.
